meeting_header: Date: 2027-06-08 10:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Location: Zoom | Redwood: Maya Patel (AE), Ethan Cole (SE), Jordan Kim (Solutions) | Customer: Sonia A., Raj M., Lena W., Tom B.
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on capacity tuning and Dedicated sizing. Ran through last week's burst rehearsal metrics, identified KV cache warmup behavior causing tail latency spikes, agreed on a 2-hour full-sim with kernel traces, and decided on next steps around pricing and SOC2 review.
topics: KV cache priming behavior and tail latency
Autoscaling policy knobs and cool-down windows
Dedicated capacity sizing and burst addendum
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone, thanks for hopping on, we're at 10:30 UTC so let's kick off, quick roll call
[00:07] Sonia: hey, hi, Sonia here, sorry a bit delayed, had to reroute through the VPN
[00:12] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood, hi all
[00:14] Raj: Raj here
[00:17] Lena: Lena — good morning
[00:20] Maya: great, agenda — run through last week's burst rehearsal metrics, dig into the p99 tail, confirm simulation plan and next steps, and pricing follow-up. Ethan you want to take us through the numbers?
[00:31] Ethan: yeah, sure. so the rehearsal we ran last thursday, we simulated steady 4k qps with two 15-minute bursts to 10k qps, overall throughput held but we saw a p99 jump during the second burst from ~180ms to 640ms, so there's a clear tail event. logs point at KV cache misses and some kernel scheduling jitter on one of the nodes.
[01:02] Raj: when you say KV cache misses, do you mean cold starts on new context keys? because our workloads have a lot of short prompts and then a few long ones that hit different token distributions
[01:12] Ethan: yeah exactly, looks like the prefix caching wasn't warming for a subset of sessions — could be batching alignment plus the autoscaler bringing up new instances during the burst, so the KV state wasn't primed. also saw some tensor core kernel fallback on one GPU during the hot window.
[01:30] Tom B.: were those nodes rebalanced by the autoscaler? we push lots of small bursts across many shards, if the cooldown is too low it might terminate before KV state hydrates
[01:41] Ethan: autoscaler cool-down was 90s in the test; we think increasing to 300-600s for dedicated pools during heavy burst windows would help. also, enabling pre-warm policy for predicted bursts — Redwood supports scheduled warmup + prefix cache priming script.
[02:00] Sonia: can we get specific — like how much more cost for longer cool-downs vs risk of p99 spikes? we need numbers for execs
[02:10] Maya: good point — I'll send a cost delta scenarios doc. for an example, increasing cool-down to 5 minutes for a 50 node pool pushes expected burn by ~6-8% during a sustained week of bursts, but it reduces incident risk. i'll include a couple of scenarios.
[02:25] Raj: another constraint — we have strict KMS policies; any burst logs that include keys need to be scrubbed. how are you handling trace export?
[02:35] Ethan: we can collect kernel traces and internal metrics with PII-free flags, and send them encrypted to your S3 with your KMS. Redwood console has a bucket-level role for trace exports; we'll only include anonymized session ids.
[02:50] Lena: Regarding SLA, list our target: p99 < 250ms for interactive flows. is that realistic for dedicated?
[02:58] Ethan: on Dedicated with warm caches and pre-warmed nodes yes, p99 < 250ms is achievable, assuming model variant selection and sequence lengths line up. cold cache or quantized kernel fallbacks can push that up.
[03:15] Speaker 1: (mumble) also need to watch tokenization differences, we saw extra tokens in the test that blew up batch sizes
[03:24] Ethan: good call — token distribution matters a lot. Raj, can you share your token length histogram?
[03:29] Raj: yes, i'll export, we'll include 50/95/99 buckets
[03:33] Maya: ok, next — simulation plan. Ethan?
[03:36] Ethan: propose a 2-hour run that mirrors peak traffic: baseline 4k qps with three aligned bursts to 12k qps for 10 minutes each, include cold-start windows, KV priming, and enable pre-warm policy. we'll capture kernel traces and per-node latency distribution. also test with and without prefix caching to see delta.
[03:55] Sonia: can you simulate our real prompt mix? we have ~70% short prompts <40 tokens and 30% longer flows 200-800 tokens
[04:04] Ethan: yes we'll parameterize that; need sample prompt set and the histogram Raj promised.
[04:10] Tom B: and please include network egress variance, last time our cloud region had throttled bandwidth and it impacted tail
[04:18] Ethan: noted — we'll introduce jitter and packet loss in the sim.
[04:22] Jordan: for the autoscaler knobs, high-level recs: increase cool-down to 5m for burst windows, use conservative scale down policy (step-down of 1 node / min), and set scale-up to be aggressive but paired with cache pre-warm. also recommend a reserve slack of 8% to absorb small surges.
[04:40] Raj: what about burst priority tiers? can we have fallback to a cheaper quantized model when Dedicated saturates?
[04:47] Maya: yes — route policy can fallback to quantized variant in a cheaper pool — we'll show cost/latency tradeoffs for that path.
[04:55] Sonia: the compliance side — we need SOC2 artifacts and SSO mapping. do you support SAML SCIM for user provisioning?
[05:03] Ethan: yes SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, and you can push audit logs to your SIEM. SOC2 report is available under NDA; we'll share the compliance pack once we have an NDA placeholder.
[05:18] Lena: what about data residency? we need EU-only storage for some patient data flows
[05:24] Maya: Redwood supports region pinning and private deployment in VPC; for PII you can use Private with on-prem or VPC controls. we'll include options and Delta on cost.
[05:33] Sonia: quick question — in the rehearsal there was a 30s blackbox period where p50 and p95 were fine but p99 spiked — any hypothesis?
[05:42] Ethan: hypothesis is twofold: (1) new node boot + cold KV cache + batch misalignment and (2) occasional kernel fallback on one GPU causing a small fraction of requests to go slow. we saw a correlated increase in GPU micro stalls in the trace.
[05:59] Raj: can you point to exact timestamps we should look at?
[06:02] Ethan: sure, I'll annotate the logs.
[06:05] Maya: ok, action items recap — Ethan will run the 2-hour sim and share traces; Maya will produce pricing scenarios; Sonia will pull compliance contacts; Raj will share histograms. Anything else?
[06:20] Sonia: one ask — can Redwood run a short live-demo of the warmup script with our prompt set? just to validate priming works
[06:28] Ethan: yes we can do a 30m lab run next week, probably Thursday morning UTC.
[06:33] Lena: worth scheduling the security deep dive soon after we get the SOC2 list
[06:38] Maya: noted. I'll loop in our security PM.
[06:42] Tom B: logging detail — can you make the traces include model variant id, node id, but not full prompt text? our legal team needs that for audit
[06:50] Ethan: yep we'll mask prompt text and include hashed session ids.
[06:54] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) cool, ok thanks
[06:58] Maya: wrap up — i'll send notes and next steps. any final questions?
[07:03] Raj: none from me
[07:05] Sonia: all good
[07:06] Lena: thanks everyone
[07:07] Maya: thanks, end call

Notes: The transcript has typical ASR errors: "KV cash" occasionally appears in the raw logs and will be corrected in engineer notes. The team agreed on 2-hour sim, a 30-minute live priming demo, and pricing + compliance artifacts to be sent.

Recap (verbatim from meeting close):
- Ethan: "I'll run the 2-hour burst sim and share kernel traces by Thursday."
- Maya: "I'll send pricing + burst addendum by Wednesday."
- Sonia: "I'll confirm SOC2 contact and compliance list."

End of transcript.
